text:
support-bot: Alert: multiple customer reports of p99 latency regressions starting ~2030 UTC after last runtime deploy. Affected: hosted + dedicated, mostly long-sequence workloads (>2048). Links: https://internal.metrics/p99-spikes :warning:

Maria G: seeing this too on internal perf tests — p50 fine, but p99 jumps 2-3x for redwood-13b quantized builds. Repro steps coming.

AJ: thanks — can you include commit hash for the deploy?

Maria G: deploy-bot logged: deploy 6b7c9a3 -> prod at 2026-03-12T02:15:12Z. That build switched default kernel selector to prefer FlashAttention on GPUs with capability >= 8.0.

Tim Lee: oh interesting. We flipped FLASH_ATTENTION default on the compiler flags last week to improve throughput. Maybe interaction with KV cache / long contexts.

Sophia H: quick triage: are errors functional or purely latency? Customers report timeouts and increased tail latency, no correctness/regression in outputs.

Kevin R: I grabbed perf traces from one affected host. Attaching snippet:```
2026-03-12T02:18:45Z model=redwood-13b seq=4096 batch=1 kernel=flash_attn forward_time_ms=42 kv_read_ms=5 attention_ms=30 other_ms=7
2026-03-12T02:19:02Z model=redwood-13b seq=4096 batch=1 kernel=sdpa forward_time_ms=18 kv_read_ms=4 attention_ms=6 other_ms=8
```
Pretty stark. FlashAttn appears ~3-4x slower for particular seq/batch than SDPA here.

AJ: that matches my local microbenchmarks: FlashAttention wins at medium sequences (<=1024) and for specific head layouts, but falls off at very long sequences because of memory copy patterns. We likely didn't gate the selector on sequence length properly.

Maria G: reproduction steps I used (local):
1) checkout 6b7c9a3
2) build runtime with same compile flags: `cmake -DUSE_FLASH=ON -DCUDA_ARCH=80 .. && make -j24`
3) run: `./bench_runner --model redwood-13b-8bit --seq 4096 --batch 1 --runs 200 --profile`
4) compare kernel timings (flash_attn vs sdpa)`

Tim Lee: can everyone run that repro quickly and paste results? I want to confirm it's deterministic and not a GC/traffic artifact.

Sophia H: ran the bench on a p4d-like node; reproduced similar: flash_attn attention_ms ~28-35ms, sdpa ~6-9ms. So not a fluke.

AJ: root cause hypothesis: the compiler's kernel choice heuristic was simplified to prefer flash on amp-compat GPUs, but it's missing a branch for seq_len > 1024 where flash kernel has poor memory locality and triggers extra device-host synchronizations when streaming KV caches. Also possible compile flags added `-DFAST_ACCUM` which changes accumulation tiling.

Kevin R: found a config diff in the build: added `-DFLASH_ATTENTION_BATCHED_KERNEL=1` in 6b7c9a3. Reverting that in a local build switches back to SDPA and fixes tails.

Maria G: mitigation options? We need something quick for customer-facing hosted API.

AJ: short term: hotfix runtime to prioritize SDPA for seq_len >= 2048 or for models with KV cache enabled. We can expose runtime flag `runtime.attention.prefer_flash = false` at roll time and flip for all tenants.

Tim Lee: alternative fast mitigation: deploy a config patch that blacklists flash kernel for redwood-13b and larger. That's lower blast radius than global rollback.

Sophia H: I'll prepare a rollout plan for a 10% canary that sets `attention.backend=sdpa` for affected model routes, monitor p95/p99 and then escalate to 100% if stable.

Maria G: customer communication: support-bot, can you open a banner and post to affected customers that we're investigating and provide ETA?

support-bot: Created incident INC-2026-3492 and banner draft saved to /support/drafts/INC-2026-3492. ETA: 2-3 hours with hotfix, will update.

Kevin R: patch snippet to force SDPA for long contexts in runtime kernel selector:```diff
- if (gpu.capability >= 80) return KERNEL_FLASH;
+ if (gpu.capability >= 80) {
+   if (seq_len >= 2048 || kv.enabled) return KERNEL_SDPA;
+   return KERNEL_FLASH;
+ }
```
We should also add a telemetry counter when we choose flash so we can track occurrences.

AJ: tests: add microbench matrix (seq=128,512,1024,2048,4096) x kernels and assert no p99 > baseline*1.5 in CI perf job.

Tim Lee: urgent PR created: https://git.internal/repo/runtime/pull/4523 — it toggles selector logic and exposes `RUNTIME_PREFER_FLASH` env var. I'm going to land to canary and roll 10% to dedicated and hosted.

Maria G: who owns the rollback plan if canary fails?

Sophia H: I'll monitor canary dashboards and have auto rollback to previous deploy on >50% p99 regression for >=5m. Deploy-bot can perform rollback.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: 10% traffic -> runtime v6b7c9a3+fix (pr-4523) at 2026-03-12T03:12:00Z.

Kevin R: also note: we should disable the aggressive compile `-DFLASH_ATTENTION_BATCHED_KERNEL=1` flag in nightly builds until we verify memory patterns. Will send a separate PR to build config.

AJ: for longer-term: instrument kernel internal metrics (memcpy counts, peak alloc, SM occupancy) and add selector cost model: choose kernel based on estimated attention cost for (seq, heads, head_dim, kv_on).

Maria G: customers responded to banner: some reported immediate improvement after canary. Others still saw tails — likely they were on different capacity or model variant. Sophia, can you expand rollout to Dedicated pools next?

Sophia H: expanding to Dedicated now (30% -> 60%). Monitoring.

support-bot: Incident INC-2026-3492 update: hotfix PR landed to canary, signs of recovery on p99 for long-seq routes. Keeping incident open while we finish rollout.

Tim Lee: follow-up action items:
- AJ: formalize patch + telemetry PR -> merge to main (owner)
- Kevin: PR to revert/disable compile flag in build config
- Sophia: rollout runbook + automated rollback thresholds
- Maria: update customer comms + postmortem draft
All: add small perf tests to CI matrix.

Maria G: thanks everyone. Learned: FlashAttention isn't universally better; kernel selection needs to be sequence-aware.

AJ: side note — for models that use long-context streaming we should prefer SDPA or hybrid kernels until we can validate flash variants across seqs. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: 100% traffic now on runtime v6b7c9a3+fix at 2026-03-12T04:20:50Z. Incident will be closed after 24h stable metrics.

support-bot: Incident INC-2026-3492 resolved: p99 restored to baseline for affected routes. Postmortem assigned to Maria G and AJ.

Maria G: starting postmortem draft now — will include timeline, root cause, customer impact, remediation, and follow-ups.

Kevin R: notes for postmortem: include microbench numbers, the compile flag diff, and the patch that gated flash by seq_len.

Sophia H: adding monitoring improvements: per-kernel p99 time series + alarm on kernel selection flips.

AJ: thanks team. Let's make the selector smarter and add a short-runner perf gate in the PR checklist so this doesn't regress again. :rocket:
